findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body: When callers invoke the returned disposer, the message handler remains registered. Subsequent messages can trigger stale or duplicate processing, and repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers indefinitely.

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned disposer
findings.body: When callers stop polling through the returned disposer, the interval remains active. `refresh` continues running every second, abandoned timers accumulate, and a live timer can prevent Node.js processes or tests from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
After any caller invokes the returned cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still call `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate active listeners and can trigger duplicate processing or listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
For every `startPolling` call, invoking the returned cleanup function leaves the interval active, so `refresh` continues running every second after cancellation. In Node.js, the referenced interval can also prevent process shutdown indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal during teardown
findings.body:
On a long-lived socket reused after logout, tenant change, or component disposal, calling the returned cleanup no longer revokes the handler. Any subsequent untrusted `"message"` event still reaches stale session logic, allowing post-teardown state access or mutation and accumulating handlers across lifecycle changes.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore removal of the registered message listener
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer detaches `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles on a long-lived socket retain every handler, causing duplicate message processing, growing memory use, and eventual listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the interval when polling is disposed
findings.body:
The returned disposer leaves the interval active. Any caller that stops or recreates polling accumulates timers and retained callback state; even one abandoned interval can keep a Node.js process alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
For every attached socket, invoking the returned cleanup function no longer calls `socket.off`. Subsequent messages still invoke the handler, breaking the exported cleanup contract and causing duplicate/stale handling after detach or reattach.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned disposer
findings.body:
For every polling session, invoking the returned cleanup function leaves the interval active. `refresh` continues running once per second after callers stop polling, and the live timer can prevent process or test shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
